snippets.output: Ringworm, also known as dermatophytosis, is a common fungal infection of the skin caused by dermatophytes.
Dermatophytes are a group of fungi that include species from the genera Trichophyton, Microsporum, and Epidermophyton.
Trichophyton, Microsporum, and Epidermophyton are genera of fungi.
These fungi thrive in warm, moist environments and can infect the skin, hair, and nails.
Transmission of ringworm occurs through direct contact with an infected person or animal, or indirectly through contact with contaminated objects.
Contaminated objects that can transmit ringworm include towels, clothing, and surfaces.
